title: Critical Transition and Pattern Scales in Shear Turbulence
exact_target: Explain why many shear flows develop large turbulent--laminar patterns close to the onset of sustained turbulence.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 30001125 (OWR-2495-002). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.
Dynamics of Patterns (2008), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2008/57, pp. 3201--3271; official report source and mathematical context.
Official EMS Press PDF of the same Oberwolfach report; PDF pages 39--40, printed pages 3239--3240.

status_qualification: This threshold is not automatically the linear-instability Reynolds number: the report stresses a discontinuous subcritical transition. It asks for the mechanism and long scale of the patterns in the examined shear flows, without a universal wavelength formula.
